title: What’s your favourite flavour of crisp?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: (idiom) something is the best and you won't find anything better
situation where one action causes many other similar actions to happen
an individual's subjective liking or disliking for something, based on their personal taste and opinion
(idiom) essential feature or element of something
relied upon to be the best thing for a particular purpose or situation
paste made of mashed avocado, lime juice and salt

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. In Britain we call them crisps and you might know them as potato chips, but whatever you call them, these fried potato slices are probably the world's favourite snack.
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Beth。在英国，我们称之为 crisps，你可能知道它们叫薯片（potato chips），但无论你怎么称呼，这些炸土豆片大概是世界上最受欢迎的零食。

sentences.en: Neil, are you a big crisp eater and what's your favourite flavour?
sentences.zh: Neil，你很爱吃薯片吗？你最喜欢的口味是什么？

sentences.en: I love crisps, Beth. They are my favourite snack.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢薯片，Beth。它们是我最喜欢的零食。

sentences.en: My favourite flavour is prawn cocktail, which is controversial because a lot of people don't like that flavour.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的口味是虾味鸡尾酒（prawn cocktail），这挺有争议的，因为很多人不喜欢那个味道。

sentences.en: I think my favourite is salt and vinegar.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我最喜欢的是盐醋味。

sentences.en: Yummy! You're making me hungry. Well, crisps might be popular but with lots of oil and salt they're not the healthiest food.
sentences.zh: 很好吃！你把我说饿了。嗯，薯片虽然很受欢迎，但含有大量的油和盐，它们并不是最健康的食物。

sentences.en: So, why do we love them so much? That's what BBC World Service programme The Food Chain wanted to find out.
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们如此热爱它们呢？这就是 BBC World Service 的节目 The Food Chain 想要探寻的。

sentences.en: Here, presenter Ruth Alexander talks to Mitchell Dingwall, a food executive responsible for developing new crisp flavours: Why do we love crisps so much?
sentences.zh: 在这里，主持人 Ruth Alexander 与负责开发薯片新口味的食品主管 Mitchell Dingwall 进行了交谈：为什么我们这么喜欢薯片？

sentences.en: Hmm. I think it's just that crunch, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯。我觉得就是那种嘎嘣脆的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: You can't beat the crunch. And then that delicious, salty feeling in your mouth and it just becomes a snowball effect.
sentences.zh: 没什么能比得上那种脆爽。然后那种美味、咸咸的感觉在嘴里蔓延，接着就产生了滚雪球效应。

sentences.en: You just want more of it! For Mitchell, the best thing about crisps is the loud crunch.
sentences.zh: 你只会想要更多！对 Mitchell 来说，薯片最棒的地方就是那响亮的嘎嘣脆声。

sentences.en: He says, " You can't beat it!" An idiom meaning something like: "That's the best thing and you won't find anything better!"
sentences.zh: 他说：“You can't beat it!” 这是一个习语，意思是：“那是最好的，你找不到比这更好的了！”

sentences.en: Mitchell says once you've started eating crisps, it's hard to stop and you just want to eat more and more.
sentences.zh: Mitchell 说，一旦你开始吃薯片，就很难停下来，你只会想越吃越多。

sentences.en: He calls this a snowball effect – a situation where doing something causes other similar things to happen.
sentences.zh: 他称之为滚雪球效应（snowball effect）——即做某事会导致其他类似事情发生的情况。

sentences.en: You eat one crisp and before you know it, the whole packet's gone!
sentences.zh: 你吃了一片薯片，不知不觉中，整包就没了！

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll be visiting two countries in love with crisps and, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将走访两个热爱薯片的国家，并且像往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新单词和短语，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有这些内容。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我有一个问题要问你，Beth。

sentences.en: The record for the world's largest packet of crisps was recently broken in Saudi Arabia, but how much did the packet weigh?
sentences.zh: 世界上最大包薯片的纪录最近在沙特阿拉伯被打破了，但这包薯片有多重呢？

sentences.en: Was it: a) about 1.5 tonnes, b) about 2.5 tonnes, or c) about 3.5 tonnes?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 大约 1.5 吨，b) 大约 2.5 吨，还是 c) 大约 3.5 吨？

sentences.en: OK. Wow! They are all huge! I'm going to guess about 3.5 tonnes.
sentences.zh: 好的。哇！都好大啊！我猜大约是 3.5 吨。

sentences.en: OK. We'll find out the answer later. Let's travel first to Singapore, home of Jolene Ng, a market research analyst who specialises in salty snacks.
sentences.zh: 好的。我们稍后会揭晓答案。让我们先去新加坡，那里是专门研究咸味零食的市场研究分析师 Jolene Ng 的家乡。

sentences.en: Here's Jolene talking with Ruth Alexander for BBC programme The Food Chain: Is the potato chip the most popular of all salty snacks?
sentences.zh: 这是 Jolene 在 BBC 节目 The Food Chain 中与 Ruth Alexander 的对话：薯片是所有咸味零食中最受欢迎的吗？

sentences.en: It's very, very much dependent on personal preference but if I were to look at certain countries, you could see, like in the UK, it's very much part and parcel of life.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上取决于个人偏好，但如果我看某些国家，你会发现，比如在英国，它完全是生活的一部分。

sentences.en: You don't have it only during snack times.
sentences.zh: 你不只是在零食时间吃它。

sentences.en: You have it with lunch as well. You put it… My husband's from the UK and he, kind of, puts it in his sandwich as well.
sentences.zh: 你午餐也会吃它。你会把它……我丈夫来自英国，他有点像是也会把它放进三明治里。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, a cheese sandwich with a crisp inside.
sentences.zh: 噢是的，夹着薯片的奶酪三明治。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, that's great! Exactly! Jolene says the popularity of different snacks depends on personal preference – someone's subjective liking or disliking for something, based on their personal opinion.
sentences.zh: 噢是的，那太棒了！没错！Jolene 说，不同零食的受欢迎程度取决于个人偏好（personal preference）——即某人基于个人观点对某事的主观喜爱或厌恶。

sentences.en: In some places, crisps are part and parcel of everyday life.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，薯片是日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Part and parcel means to be an essential element or feature of something.
sentences.zh: Part and parcel 的意思是成为某事的重要组成部分或特征。

sentences.en: In Britain, crisps are so essential that people even eat crisp sandwiches!
sentences.zh: 在英国，薯片是如此重要，以至于人们甚至吃薯片三明治！

sentences.en: But not everywhere is so in love with potato chips.
sentences.zh: 但并非到处都如此热爱薯片。

sentences.en: Let's meet Jenny Martinez, a food vlogger from Mexico.
sentences.zh: 让我们认识一下来自墨西哥的美食博主 Jenny Martinez。

sentences.en: In Mexico, tortilla corn chips are eaten instead of potato chips, and it's common to see street vendors selling bags of corn tortillas filled with different sauces.
sentences.zh: 在墨西哥，人们吃玉米片（tortilla corn chips）而不是薯片，经常可以看到街头小贩在卖装满各种酱料的袋装玉米片。

sentences.en: Here, Jenny tells Ruth Alexander more for BBC World Service programme The Food Chain: For you, which is your go-to snack – the tortilla chip or the potato chip?
sentences.zh: 在这里，Jenny 在 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 中告诉 Ruth Alexander 更多信息：对你来说，哪种是你首选的零食——玉米片还是薯片？

sentences.en: Definitely the tortilla chip. Why? Because you could do so many things – dip it in almost everything, adding some guacamole,spicy salsa or just sour cream with a mixture of chipotle sauce.
sentences.zh: 绝对是玉米片。为什么？因为你可以做很多尝试——几乎可以蘸任何东西，加点牛油果酱（guacamole）、辣萨尔萨酱，或者只是酸奶油混合烟熏辣椒酱。

sentences.en: Ruth asks if tortillas are Jenny's go-to snack.
sentences.zh: Ruth 问玉米片是否是 Jenny 的首选（go-to）零食。

sentences.en: You can use the phrase go-to to describe something which is relied upon to be the best thing for a particular purpose.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用 go-to 这个短语来描述为了特定目的而被认为最可靠、最好的东西。

sentences.en: For example, for a lot of people, Wikipedia is the go-to website for online information.
sentences.zh: 例如，对很多人来说，维基百科是获取在线信息的首选网站。

sentences.en: And Jenny thinks corn tortillas are especially good with guacamole, a paste made of mashed avocado… which sounds delicious and maybe a little healthier than a British crisp sandwich!
sentences.zh: Jenny 认为玉米片配上牛油果酱（guacamole）特别棒，那是一种用捣碎的牛油果制成的酱……听起来很美味，而且可能比英国的薯片三明治更健康一点！

sentences.en: Speaking of which, what was the answer to your question, Neil?
sentences.zh: 说到这个，Neil，你那个问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: I asked you how heavy the world's largest bag of crisps was.
sentences.zh: 我问你世界上最大包的薯片有多重。

sentences.en: And I said very heavy – over three and a half tonnes.
sentences.zh: 而我说是非常重——超过 3.5 吨。

sentences.en: Well, it's not that big but the real answer is still enormous – about 1.5 tonnes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没那么大，但真正的答案依然惊人——大约 1.5 吨。

sentences.en: The bag, made in Riyadh, was nine metres tall.
sentences.zh: 这包在利雅得制作的薯片有九米高。

sentences.en: Yeah. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrase you can't beat that, meaning that something is the best and you won't find anything better.
sentences.zh: 是的。好了。让我们回顾一下学过的词汇，从短语 you can't beat that 开始，意思是某样东西是最好的，你找不到比它更好的了。

sentences.en: A snowball effect is a situation where one action causes other similar actions to happen.
sentences.zh: 滚雪球效应（snowball effect）是指一个动作引起其他类似动作发生的情况。

sentences.en: Someone's personal preference is their subjective liking or disliking for something, based on their own opinion.
sentences.zh: 个人的偏好（personal preference）是某人基于自己的观点对某事的主观喜爱或厌恶。

sentences.en: To be part and parcel of something means to be an essential or integral feature of it.
sentences.zh: 成为某事的 part and parcel 意味着它是该事物必不可少的或不可分割的特征。

sentences.en: And something which is described as the go-to can be relied upon as the best thing for a particular situation.
sentences.zh: 被描述为 go-to 的东西可以被视为特定情况下最可靠、最好的选择。

sentences.en: And finally, guacamole is a paste made of mashed avocado, lime juice and salt – delicious!
sentences.zh: 最后，guacamole 是一种由捣碎的牛油果、青柠汁和盐制成的酱——非常美味！

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up but if you're hungry for more, then head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you'll find a worksheet and quiz for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但如果你还想了解更多，请前往我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，在那里你可以找到本期节目的练习单和测验。

sentences.en: See you again soon, but for now, goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快会再见，但现在，再见！

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
